opsec.config.title: OpSec Enhanced Settings
opsec.section.restartWarning: §e⚠ Requires game restart to take effect
opsec.button.randomizeSkin.tooltip: Uploads a procedurally-generated flat-color skin as your active skin (a random model variant too). Not pulled from any external site - generated locally, so there's nothing to vet for consent or licensing. Also useful if the Skin/Cape Correlation Alert flagged two of your accounts for sharing a skin.
opsec.button.randomizeCape.tooltip: Picks a random cape from the ones this account actually owns (including 'no cape' as an option). Capes can't be granted from outside - only capes Mojang already gave this account can be selected.
opsec.appearanceRandomizer.unavailable: §7Log into a Microsoft account below to randomize its skin/cape
opsec.option.spoofAsVanilla.tooltip:
On: enable client spoofing - pick which client to spoof as below, and block ALL other mod(s) from detection
Off: advertise as real Fabric brand and optionally allow some mod(s)
opsec.brandOverride.vanilla.tooltip: Advertise the plain 'vanilla' brand. Always accurate, always allowed by any server that accepts vanilla.
opsec.brandOverride.lunar.tooltip: Advertise as Lunar Client (brand string + no mod channels, matching Lunar's own vanilla-like network behavior). Does not emulate Lunar's proprietary cosmetics protocol, so a server that specifically probes for it may still notice. Only helps on servers that allowlist 'lunarclient' but reject plain vanilla - an uncommon setup. Version suffix can be kept current by editing 'lunarVersionSuffix' in opsec.json.
opsec.brandOverride.badlion.tooltip: Advertise as Badlion Client (brand string + no mod channels, matching Badlion's own vanilla-like network behavior). No version number involved, so this can't go stale. Only helps on servers that allowlist Badlion but reject plain vanilla - an uncommon setup.
opsec.option.dpiFragmentTls.tooltip: Splits the TLS ClientHello of this mod's own update-check / integrity-check requests across two TCP segments, to dodge naive SNI-based connection blocking (relevant in Russia/China/Iran). Does NOT cover Microsoft/Xbox login (different network stack) or the game connection itself (not TLS) - pair with a system-level tool like zapret/GoodbyeDPI/ByeDPI for those. Off by default.
opsec.option.compactLayout.tooltip: Tighter row spacing in this settings menu. Purely cosmetic, takes effect immediately.
opsec.option.showHud.tooltip: Shows a small always-on-screen label with the current spoof brand in the top-left corner. Purely cosmetic. Not yet available on 26.1+.
opsec.option.serverProfile.tooltip: ON: save a snapshot of your current settings just for this server address, editable independently of your global defaults. OFF: delete the snapshot and go back to your global defaults. Only shown while the config screen is opened with an active connection (e.g. via Mod Menu's in-game menu) - the multiplayer-list button opens before any server is chosen.
opsec.option.whitelistMode.locked.toolti: Locked to 'Block All' because Spoof as Vanilla is on
opsec.whitelist.mode.auto.tooltip: Mods with network channels are automatically whitelisted
opsec.whitelist.mode.custom.tooltip: Manually select which mods to whitelist
opsec.packstrip.mode.manual.tooltip: Default vanilla behavior on push. You can still toggle any server pack
opsec.packstrip.mode.ask.tooltip: Server resource pack not applied but with consent screen to ask if the pack(s) should be applied
opsec.packstrip.mode.alwaysOn.tooltip: Server resource pack not applied by default. You can still toggle any server pack
opsec.packstrip.title: Server Resource Pack
opsec.packstrip.required: This server has a required resource pack.
opsec.packstrip.optional: This server has an optional resource pack.
opsec.packstrip.stripped: §7OpSec bypassed this pack's content. You may apply it below.
opsec.chatguard.title: OpSec: Confirm Action
opsec.chatguard.message.command:
This message wants to run this command on your behalf:
%s

Only continue if you trust the sender.
opsec.chatguard.message.clipboard:

%s

This link looks like a phishing/IP-grabber pattern (raw IP, punycode, or look-alike characters):

The real destination will be shown again next — check it carefully before opening.

opsec.option.guardChatLinks.tooltip: Require confirmation before a clicked chat/sign/book message copies text to your clipboard or runs a command. Vanilla executes both instantly with no prompt.
